newsitem.title: JAPAN: Consumer doubts cast shadow on Japan economy--EPA.
newsitem.headline: Consumer doubts cast shadow on Japan economy--EPA.

text.p: Japan's economy continues to recover, although a haze of uncertainty has descended over the health of consumer demand, the government said in its monthly economic report on Friday.
The Economic Planning Agency (EPA) said in its overall assessment that while the tempo remained slow, the economy was recovering on the back of strong capital spending and housing starts.
The assessment, closely watched for signs of shifts in economic policy, was unchanged from the previous month.
The report also said consumer demand was recovering gradually but an EPA official added that "there are elements which need to be looked at cautiously".
Private economists consider the strength of consumer demand as one of the key factors which will decide the strength of Japan's economy in fiscal 1997/98, starting on April 1.

The sales tax will be raised to five percent from three percent on April 1, and while a consumer buying spree is expected in February and March, a petering out of demand is also expected in the April-June quarter.
The official said, however, that the expected buying spree seemed to be confined to certain types of large purchases.
"The rush to buy is so far only obvious in cars and housing. It is not as though consumers have been swept up in a buying frenzy," he said.
Wage growth of 0.5 percent year-on-year in December was lower than expected and slightly worrying, he said. But he added that this might just reflect delays in winter bonus payments.
Looking ahead, the official said industrial production in February would be affected by the fire at a Toyota Motor Corp car parts supplier's factory last weekend.
He said while it was difficult to judge the extent of the impact, it was unlikely to be dramatic enough to change the overall rising trend of industrial output.

Car production represented 7.2 percent of output in the October-December period, of which Toyota's output was about one-third -- which would lop 0.1 percent off industrial output for every day Toyota's production lines were idle, he said.
The Trade Ministry has forecast that industrial output by manufacturers will fall 2.9 percent in February after rising 4.9 percent in January.

The fire last Saturday at a plant of Aisin Seiki Co Ltd prevented output of brake parts supplied to Toyota, forcing the idling of all the carmaker's domestic plants on Tuesday, except for those of Daihatsu Motor Co Ltd.
Toyota said on Friday that production has resumed at all its domestic plants.
